jobs.prompt:
ci(cpp): make the C++ gateway full-suite workflow run, and run it on agent result branches

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
Branch `claude/cpp-gateway-port` contains `cpp/gateway/`, a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway with 441 test binaries. Read `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` first: `cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh` (a wrapper for `cpp/gateway/cmake/ci/driver.py`) is a portable build-and-test driver for disposable runners. The workflow `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-ci.yml` is meant to build the whole gateway in release mode on GitHub's `ubuntu-26.04-arm` runner and run the full suite in four shards. Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM.

CURRENT STATE (observed)
The workflow's first run failed in all four shards within seconds, at the step "Build and test":
`cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh: Permission denied` (exit 126): the script is committed without the executable bit. Nothing after that line has ever run in CI, so more problems are likely behind it. Known candidates: (1) since the driver was written, the tree gained vendored libraries under `cpp/gateway/third_party/` (simdjson, simdutf) that first-party sources include, registered in `cpp/gateway/CMakeLists.txt`, `cpp/gateway/tools/vendor_sources.py` and `cpp/gateway/cmake/vendors.json`; check that the driver compiles and links them (third-party code is compiled without the port's `-Werror` warning set; with Clang, headers included by tree path need `--system-header-prefix=third_party/`); (2) the driver was qualified with GCC 14, the workflow uses Clang 21 from Ubuntu 26.04 (`CXX=clang++`); (3) a few tests assert ARM64-only platform contracts; on the ARM64 runner they should pass.

TASK
1. Fix the workflow so it works: invoke the driver through `bash` (or set the executable bit in git with `git update-index --chmod=+x`; do both), and fix whatever else stops the driver from building and testing the current tree.
2. Extend the workflow triggers so the same four-shard suite also runs on pushes to branches matching `agent-jobs/**` (result branches of automated agents) and on pull requests targeting `claude/cpp-gateway-port`. Keep `permissions: contents: read`, keep `persist-credentials: false`, do not add secrets, do not add any step that pushes or comments. Keep concurrency per ref with cancel-in-progress.
3. Make each shard upload the driver's result files and logs as an artifact (the current `path` globs found nothing: point them at what the driver really writes under `UOS_CI_BUILD_DIR`), and write a short job summary (`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`): binaries built, binaries passed/failed, cases passed/failed, names of failing tests.
4. Prove it as far as your runner allows. Your runner is x64 Ubuntu 26.04 (borrowed compute; the product is ARM64): install the packages the workflow installs (`clang ninja-build pkg-config mold util-linux libboost-json-dev libboost-container-dev libssl-dev libsqlite3-dev zlib1g-dev libicu-dev libbrotli-dev libzstd-dev`), build SQLite 3.54.0 exactly as the workflow does, then run `CXX=clang++ UOS_CI_JOBS=4 bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release --shard 1/4` and at least one more shard to completion. On x64 the documented ARM64-only fixtures fail by design (see `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-ci-build-x86-20261117.md`); everything else must build and pass. Fix driver problems in `cpp/gateway/cmake/ci/` and `cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh`. If a TEST fails for a reason that is not the driver or the platform, do not change the test or the production source: list it in your report with the first error lines.
After your branch is pushed, the workflow itself will run on it on ARM64 (because of the new `agent-jobs/**` trigger); the maintainer reads that run as the acceptance evidence.

OWNED PATHS (you may create or edit only these)
- `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-ci.yml`
- `cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh`, `cpp/gateway/cmake/ci/*.py`, `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md`
- `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-ci-workflow-20261118.md` (your report: what was wrong, what you changed, exact commands, real counts per shard you ran, anything that still fails and why)

RULES
- Do not edit any other workflow, the TypeScript, production C++ sources or tests.
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file.
- Commit small steps often (model connections can drop); keep the report current. Leave no build output in the checkout.

DONE WHEN
`CXX=clang++ UOS_CI_JOBS=4 bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release --shard 1/4` builds and runs on your runner with only the documented ARM64-only fixture failures, the workflow file is valid YAML with the triggers above, and the report states the counts.
